newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Wing of Burundi's Hutu party threatens force.
newsitem.headline: Wing of Burundi's Hutu party threatens force.

text.p: A wing of Burundi's Hutu-dominated Frodebu party threatened on Tuesday to resort to force to restore constitutional rule and said it was shameful military ruler Pierre Buyoya was invited to an African summit.
The wing led by Jean Minani said in a statement that if the international community and Organisation of African Unity (OAU) failed, "the Frodebu party will use all means including military struggle".
It appealed to the OAU and United Nations to urge the U.N. Security Council to take action including an arms embargo and the condemnation and isolation of Buyoya's military-appointed government.
He said the OAU invitation to Buyoya was "a shame for the African continent".
Minani and some followers fled to Dar es Salaam in Tanzania shortly after Buyoya seized power from Burundi's Hutu civilian president in a coup last July and banned political parties.
A rival wing of Frodebu in exile then emerged and elected Hutu rebel leader Leonard Nyangoma as its leader. Nyangoma is the leader of Hutu rebels fighting the Tutsi-dominated army.

The OAU has invited Buyoya to its annual summit in Harare from next Monday. Regional East and Central African states eased sanctions on Burundi last month after Buyoya revealed his government had held secret talks with Nyangoma's Hutu rebels.

More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels since the killing of Burundi's first elected Hutu president in 1993 by Tutsi troops.
